visual_action: The video displays gameplay from a farming simulation game, showing a blue tractor harvesting a large green field. Throughout the video, various still images and graphics are superimposed over the gameplay. These include a photo of Donald Trump at a podium holding a chart, a bar graph showing a decline in 'U.S. soybean sales to China', the flag of China, a news graphic from 'News Nation' detailing the drop in Chinese soybean purchases from the U.S., and a photo of Donald Trump and Javier Milei giving thumbs-up in front of American and Argentinian flags.

cast.name: Donald Trump
cast.evidence: He is shown in multiple photos and is the subject of the entire spoken narration, which begins 'Trump once said...' and critiques his trade policies.

cast.name: China
cast.evidence: Mentioned throughout the narration in the context of the trade war and soybean sales. The flag of China is also shown on screen.

cast.name: Brazil
cast.evidence: Mentioned in the narration as a country where China started buying soybeans from.

cast.name: Argentina
cast.evidence: Mentioned in the narration as a country China bought soybeans from and as the recipient of a bailout from Trump.

cast.name: Javier Milei
cast.evidence: Shown in a photograph with Donald Trump, standing in front of US and Argentinian flags.

cast.name: News Nation
cast.evidence: The logo for 'NEWS NATION' appears on a graphic about soybean sales.

on_screen_text.text: All soybean sales to Chinese companies ceased at the end of May.
U.S. LOSES OUT ON BILLIONS IN SOYBEAN SALES

spoken_summary: A narrator argues that Donald Trump's claim that "trade wars are good and easy to win" is false, citing the decline of the U.S. soybean industry as proof. The narrator explains that after Trump imposed tariffs on China and China retaliated, Chinese buyers began purchasing soybeans from Brazil and Argentina. As a result, U.S. soybean sales to China have allegedly dropped to zero, hurting American farmers. The video concludes by criticizing Trump for giving a "20 billion dollar bailout to Argentina" and questions why he isn't "putting America first."
audio_music: A steady, rhythmic instrumental track plays throughout the video. It serves as neutral background music. Two sound effects are used: a 'cash register' sound when the narrator says 'prices went up,' and a 'Bruh' sound effect after stating that the U.S. is now selling 'zero soybeans to China.'
editing_pacing: The video uses continuous B-roll footage from a video game with overlaid still images, graphics, and text that appears word-by-word, synchronized with the narration. The pacing is consistent and driven by the spoken audio.
central_claim: Donald Trump's trade war with China has failed, devastated the American soybean industry, and he is now prioritizing foreign countries like Argentina over American farmers.
intended_effect: To persuade viewers that Trump's trade policies are harmful to American farmers and contradict his 'America First' slogan.
